title: Preparation and Implantation of Alzet Pumps
author: Michael W. Manning
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iyacfse
materials: PREPARATION of ALZET Osmotic Pumps for Subcutaneous Implantation
Surgical Implantation of Mini-Osmotic & Micro-Osmotic Pumps
Surgical Implantation of Mini-Osmotic & Micro-Osmotic Pumps

steps.title: Design Experiment and Calculate Dosages
steps.instruction: Determine the infusion length (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 6, or 12 weeks) and infusion rate (e.g., AngII 500 ng/kg/min or 1,000 ng/kg/min). Weigh mice to ensure they are ≥ 20 g. Use a Microsoft Excel worksheet template to calculate the required amount of reagent (e.g., AngII) and sterile saline based on body weight.

steps.title: Prepare Reagent Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the reagent solution under a cell culture hood using sterile plastic tubes (do not use glass for AngII due to high affinity).

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate AngII vial to room temperature before opening.
Weigh the calculated amount of AngII into a sterile plastic tube and record the lot number.
Add the calculated volume of sterile saline to the lyophilized AngII, cap, and mix thoroughly until clear.
Label sterile Eppendorf tubes (0.5 - 1.5 ml) with mouse numbers.
Pipette the calculated amount of sterile saline and AngII solution into each Eppendorf tube based on the Excel worksheet calculations.
Prepare and label sterile plastic test tubes (4 ml) for pump incubation.

steps.title: Fill Osmotic Pumps
steps.instruction: Fill the osmotic pumps (ALZET 2001, 2004, 2006 or 1004) while wearing gloves to prevent skin oils from damaging the pump casings.

substeps.instruction: Open only the required number of pumps and flow regulators; record the lot number.
Weigh each pump (main body and flow regulator) individually to 4 decimal places to determine the 'empty weight'.
Place each weighed pump in a weight boat marked with the mouse number.
Attach a filling needle to a 1 cc sterile syringe and draw AngII solution from the Eppendorf tube, minimizing air bubbles.
Invert the syringe with the needle aimed at the floor to prevent bubbles from entering the pump.
Gently insert the filling needle into the pump body, ensuring the tip does not rest tightly on the bottom.
Fill the pump slowly until a bead of fluid rises out of the pump body, then stop.
Remove the needle/syringe and draw up any excess fluid from the pump body.
Insert the flow regulator tightly into the pump body and blot any leaking fluid.
Weigh the filled pump to determine the 'fill weight'.
Calculate fill volume: Filling volume = fill weight - empty weight (assuming 1 µl = 1 µg).
Compare the calculated volume to the mean fill volume indicated in the lot instructions.

steps.title: Incubate and Prime Pumps
steps.instruction: Prime the pumps in sterile saline before implantation.

substeps.instruction: Place the filled pump into a labeled 4 ml sterile test tube with the regulator head facing UPWARDS.
Add enough sterile saline to cover the pump.
Incubate test tubes at 37 ºC.
For Alzet 2004 model, incubate overnight (at least 12 hours) for partial priming (pumping starts 24 hours post-surgery).
If continuous infusion is required immediately after a first pump's removal, incubate pumps at 37 ºC for > 40 hours (for Alzet 2004).

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Equipment
steps.instruction: Sterilize and organize all surgical tools and the workspace.

substeps.instruction: Place gauze and cotton swabs on a surgical drape, fold corner to corner, and secure with autoclave tape. Wrap with another drape and tape.
Place surgical tools (scissors, hemostat, forceps, staples, and stapler) in sterilization pouches and seal.
Autoclave both packs in a dry cycle.
Fill Isoflurane and set up the induction box in the prep area and the nose cone in the clean area of the laminar flow hood.
Set up betadine, 70% ethanol, sterile water, bead sterilizer, hand cleaner, swabs, gauze, and pumps in the laminar hood.

steps.title: Perform Pump Implantation
steps.instruction: Surgically implant the pump under anesthesia in a sterile environment.

substeps.instruction: Surgeon puts on mask and gown, opens the outer drape, puts on sterile gloves, and opens the inside pack.
Set up the sterile drape with the nose cone in the laminar flow hood.
Place mouse in the induction chamber; once anesthetized, shave the area over the shoulder.
Place mouse in the laminar hood with the nose cone, head pointing toward the dominant hand.
Swab and wipe the area three times with betadine, then with 70% ethanol.
Make a 1 cm incision behind the ear over the shoulder blade of the front leg, perpendicular to the tail, cutting only the skin.
Use forceps to open the incision and a straight hemostat to create a subcutaneous tunnel toward the tail.
Create a pump pocket by opening the hemostat jaws under the skin, then withdraw the hemostat.
Insert the pump regulator head first into the incision (pointing toward the tail) and push completely into the pocket.
Pinch both sides of the incision and secure with staples, ensuring complete wound closure.
Apply Topical 4% Lidocaine cream with a clean swab.

steps.title: Post-Operative Care and Recovery
steps.instruction: Monitor the mice and maintain sterility between procedures.

substeps.instruction: Between mice: place instruments in a bead sterilizer for 10 seconds, dip in sterile water, and allow to cool; clean hands with antiseptic handrub.
Return mouse to cage and monitor until full recovery is achieved.
Fill the post-operation card and monitor mice closely for 7 days post-surgery.
Remove wound clips between 10-14 days.
